transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
Live from NPR News, I'm Giles Snyder.
A California proposition to establish a first in the nation wealth tax has failed.
That's according to a race call by the Associated Press or if it's jailed, a member station KQED reports.
California's Proposition 40 would have imposed a one-time 5% wealth tax on the state's billionaires.
Around 53% of voters opposed it.
Prop 40 was backed by a health care workers' union, and most of the revenue would have been used to fund health care.
Opponents, including Governor Gavin Newsom, said the tax would ultimately hurt the state's budget.
The state's billionaires fought the measure hard.
Google co-founder Sir Gabrielle funneled over $100 million into two measures designed to cancel out the wealth tax.
For NPR News, I'm Laura Fitzgerald in San Francisco.
President Trump says the FBI is investigating NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang,
but during a White House briefing, Trump said he does not think Huang has anything to worry about.
The company announced over the weekend that it's investigating whether Huang was a target of a foreign intelligence effort
after he acknowledged an extramarital affair with a woman suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
And here's John Ruich.
I think we can expect scrutiny from Congress on this.
You know, Jensen Huang's already been summoned by three House committees to brief them on the matter.
One of the big questions to watch is going to be what the government knew and when.
That's because some of the reporting around this says intelligence agencies told senior officials,
including President Trump, about this a year or so ago.
And then President Trump's going to China next week for an Asia-Pacific summit
where he's going to have talks with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
So it'll be interesting to see how this all plays out there.
And here's John Ruich reporting NVIDIA shares dropped more than 4% Monday.
Defense Secretary Pete Hexeth is planning to hold a news conference in the morning,
his first from the Pentagon in six months.
He told reporters Monday that he will address the impeachment resolution against him
filed by outgoing Kentucky Republican Congressman Thomas Massey.
Trump administration trying to restart peace talks between Ukraine and Russia,
peace negotiations taking place in Abu Dhabi.
And they come the week before Trump is set to depart for Asia,
where Trump may meet with the Russian leader.
Here's NPR's Deepa Shivaraj.
Trump heads to the Philippines and China next week for two summits, ASEAN and APEC.
At the APEC summit in China, Trump will again meet with Chinese leader Xi Jinping.
It's also possible he holds a trilateral meeting with both Xi and Russian leader Vladimir Putin,
though such a meeting has not been confirmed.
Trump said Sunday if the meeting happens, it will be "interesting."
He wants to discuss denuclearization and the end to the war in Iran.
Trump's trip comes after his party faced significant losses in the midterm elections.
Now he'll be using his last two years as president to try and firm up his legacy,
both at home and abroad.
Deepa Shivaraj, NPR News.
And you're listening to NPR News.
A new report warns roughly one in five people in Lebanon face crisis levels of food insecurity
as "continuing violence and economic hardship" hamper the country's recovery.
From Beirut, NPR's Sharad Rizkalb reports.
The Integrated Food Security Phase Classification, or IPC,
is a globally used system for assessing the severity of food insecurity.
It says around 20% of people in Lebanon are experiencing crisis levels of food insecurity.
The report attributes this to the commutative impact of two wars in less than two years,
compounded by a fragile economy and rising living costs.
Despite the U.S.-brokered cease-fire, Israeli strikes continue in southern Lebanon
near the areas occupied and raised by Israeli forces.
Lebanese state media says they're happening daily.
The IPC says the ongoing insecurity has further undermined households' ability
to recover from previous losses, displacement, and disruptions to their lives.
Jua'ad Rizkalb, NPR News, Beirut.
The Supreme Court has cleared the way for border wall construction
to resume in the Big Bend region of West Texas.
The court Monday granted the Trump administration's emergency request
to lift a federal judge's order that blocked construction while a lawsuit plays out.
Opponents argue that the project wastes money
in an area with historically low illegal immigration.
The Food and Drug Administration is requiring drugmakers
to add a new warning to the labels of popular GLP-1 weight loss drugs.
The FDA says there is a potential of increased risk of a serious eye condition
that could result in vision loss so it occurs in only a fraction of patients.
I'm Giles Snyder. This is NPR News.
